why:
The London is your opening as White. You play d4 and bring the c1 bishop to f4 early. Then you play e3, Nf3, Nbd2, c3 and Bd3, and you castle short. You use the same set-up against most Black replies.

In most lines the bishop goes to f4 before you play e3. The e3 pawn would shut the c1 bishop in. On f4 the bishop stays outside your pawns and controls the b8-h2 diagonal.

Your pawns on c3, d4 and e3 are the base. Black attacks d4 with ...c5 and ...Nc6. The c3 pawn, the e3 pawn and the f3 knight guard it.

The opening asks for patience. You learn one set-up and a few ideas. You do not need long lines. Watch for ...c5 and ...Qb6. The first attacks d4. The second attacks b2.

The London connects to your other openings. In the Slav, the pawn on e6 can shut your c8 bishop in. In the London, the pawn on e3 can shut your c1 bishop in. In both openings the bishop comes out first. The Caro-Kann uses the same idea.

variations.middlegame:
You have finished the set-up. The pawn on d4 is attacked twice and guarded three times, so keep those guards.

Your first plan is Ne5. In the tree, Black plays ...Bb7. Then you can play Ne5. The d4 pawn and the g3 bishop guard e5. If Black takes with ...Nxe5, retake with dxe5. The pawn attacks the d6 bishop and the f6 knight, and you win a piece.

Your second plan is the e4 break. The d3 bishop and the d2 knight support it. A typical order is Re1, Qe2 and then e4. The e4 pawn attacks d5.

If Black trades with ...Bxg3, retake with hxg3. Then the h-file is half open. Keep the plan: Re1, Qe2 and e4.

mistakes.text: Move 2 is Bf4, not e3. The e3 pawn shuts in the c1 bishop. The bishop can then go only to d2. This is not a blunder, but it breaks your plan.
Retake with the h-pawn, not the f-pawn. After fxg3 you have doubled pawns on g2 and g3. After hxg3 the h-file is half open for your rook. This is not a blunder, but it breaks your plan.
Play Nbd2, not Nc3. The knight on c3 blocks your own c-pawn. Then c3 is not free for your pawn when ...c5 comes. This is not a blunder, but it breaks your plan.
